deep.reconstruction:
The page has one coloured diagram headed by the ordered list of four involutions 'σ1 σ σ2 σ0'. On p.137 Grothendieck studies 'repères' (flags or frames) attached to oriented pseudolines D of a pseudoline system, in a 'fuseau de croisement' (crossing spindle). There σ2 is the involution reversing the orientation of D and σ0 is still uncertain ('σ0 = ?'). On p.139 he works out a toy case with 2 vertices, 1 face, 2 edges and 4 repères (the sides a±, b± of two edges). There σ0 = σ2 =: σ' commutes with σ, and σ1 = σσ'. He then compares this with the cartographic triple (σ0', σ1', σ2') of the barycentric subdivision.

So the setting is a set of repères with four involutions σ1, σ, σ2, σ0: the usual cartographic triple (σ0, σ1, σ2) of a map, plus a fourth involution σ tied to the crossing or orientation data.

The diagram is the planar (Schlegel-type) picture of the complete graph K4 on these four generators, with each of its 6 edges subdivided at a midpoint labelled by a pair (σi,σj). The outer arc carries the edge σ1–σ0 through (σ1,σ0). Arrows run from each generator σi to each pair vertex (σi,σj) containing it. From outside, each product σiσj sends an arrow into (σi,σj). The six products drawn are σ1σ2, σ1σ, σ0σ2, σσ2, σσ0 and σ1σ0; the one from σσ2 is dashed.

This is the natural diagram of the subgroup lattice of rank ≤2 generated by the involutions: ⟨σi⟩ ⊂ ⟨σi,σj⟩ ⊃ ⟨σiσj⟩. Equivalently it is the diagram of the corresponding orbit sets (quotients of the set of repères), with maps from finer to coarser quotients. Geometrically it is the boundary of the 'tetrahedron of types' in a 4-generator (rank-3) reflection-type structure: generators correspond to faces, pairs to edges, and the products σiσj to the rotations around edges, whose orders are the edge data.

There are also arrows between pair vertices, i.e. some edges of the medial octahedron:
- (σ1,σ) → (σ1,σ2)
- (σ,σ2) → (σ1,σ2)
- (σ,σ2) → (σ,σ0)
- (σ2,σ0) → (σ,σ0)

These can only be inclusions or orbit maps if extra relations hold. An example is the relation of p.139, where σ = σ1σ2 ∈ ⟨σ1,σ2⟩ and σ0 = σ2. So the arrows presumably record which dihedral orbit structures factor through others in the pseudoline situation. The colour coding (orange vs yellow-green) seems to separate two kinds of pair; one reading is the 'genuine' cells of the map versus the auxiliary ones involving σ. This cannot be decided from the page alone. The purpose is bookkeeping: organising which orbit sets (vertices, edges, faces, crossings, 'fuseaux') of the enriched flag structure map to which, before the explicit computation on p.139.
errors: No errors as such. The diagram is a scratch bookkeeping figure. The arrows between pair vertices are not justified by subgroup inclusion for four free involutions and require unstated relations (such as σ = σ1σ2 or σ0 = σ2, as on p.139). The colour convention is not explained, and the dashed arrow from σσ2 suggests a hesitation.

ideas.what: Encoding a cell structure (pseudoline arrangement with crossing and orientation data) by a set of flags/repères acted on by involutions, extending the cartographic triple σ0, σ1, σ2 by a fourth involution σ
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group / flag-graph or 'gem' encoding of maps and polytopes; 4 involutions as in rank-3 maps or maniplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (cartographic group, Esquisse 1984); Jones–Singerman (1978) for maps; Lins / Ferri–Gagliardi (crystallisations, 1980s); Wilson; maniplexes (Wilson 2012)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), cartographic groups in dimension 2 and the remark on higher dimensions; application to pseudolines unpublished

ideas.what: Diagram of rank-1 and rank-2 subgroups ⟨σi⟩, ⟨σiσj⟩ ⊂ ⟨σi,σj⟩ drawn as the subdivided K4 / tetrahedron boundary
ideas.modern_name: Coxeter diagram / parabolic subgroup lattice; complex of groups over the tetrahedron of types

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to describe pseudoline systems (with crossing spindles and orientations) by a four-involution 'cartographic' structure σ1, σ, σ2, σ0 on repères. This is an alternative combinatorial encoding of pseudoline arrangements, not the usual wiring-diagram or oriented-matroid encoding. It is left at the stage of a bookkeeping diagram and a toy example.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only mildly interesting. Flag-graph or maniplex style encodings of pseudoline arrangements, including the extra orientation-reversal involution, could link Grothendieck's dessins/cartographic viewpoint to oriented-matroid rank-3 combinatorics. The page itself contains no result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a scratch diagram of subgroup and orbit inclusions for four involutions. The method is standard (Coxeter / cartographic-group bookkeeping), and its application to pseudolines is only suggested, with no new result on the page.
transcription_corrections: The label of the top-middle pair vertex is written '(σ1, σ2)' with a corrected or overwritten σ2; it should read (σ1,σ2).
The bottom-left generator vertex is σ (with the label partly hidden by the dot); the pair below centre is (σ,σ0); the centre vertex is (σ,σ2).
The arrow from σσ2 to (σ,σ2) is the dashed orange one; the arrow from σσ0 to (σ,σ0) is solid green.
The arc at the top carries σ1σ0 → (σ1,σ0), with arcs from σ1 and σ0 converging there.
